title: A sibling Go sync tells an agent to run make repin, which moves every pin to main
foundBy: deps-maintenance campaign, pilots 1 and 2: the pilot2 orchestrator's findings (campaign-workspaces/deps-maintenance/pilot2/archives/deps-pilot2-20260922T203209Z/orchestrator/output/findings.md) and the step corrections pilot3's coordination.md section 5 carries

evidence.verified:
`make ci` passed at 10cc896, with 111 unit tests where main had 95, and with the end-to-end run of the action. `test_a_sibling_pin_moves_to_its_head_commit_and_nothing_else` fails on the old code.

The collector's run of 2026-09-22T22:07:49Z over all nine projects emits no `make repin`. Each of its 23 Go syncs runs `go get -tool <command>@<lag.head> && go mod tidy`.

The dashboards action syncing ledger ran verbatim in a clean clone and exited 0. Then `go tool cs-ledger version` printed the pseudo-version of the commit the report names. `git status` showed `go.mod` and `go.sum`, and `make check` passed.

resolution: A Go sync moves one pin to the commit in `lag.head`, in each module file that pins it, and nothing else.
details: Every Go `sync` action emits `make repin` as its one step. That target moves every sibling pin at once, so it cannot make one action as one commit. It resolves `@latest`, so it cannot reach the commit the action names in `lag.head`. In a campaign it pins a sibling's base instead of its frozen commit, and pilot2's qa measured it pinning lint's base. The step that makes one action is `go get <module>@<lag.head>` followed by `go mod tidy`.

notes.text: Moving a sibling to its newest commit also raises any pin that commit requires. In dashboards the ledger sync moved the lint pin too, because ledger now requires a newer lint. That is minimal version selection, and the campaign's pin rules already say to select the other action first.
